mainEntity.name: How much does a MINI Clubman Cooper D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the engine code and condition. For the 1.6L 9HZ engine, rebuilt units typically range from £2,000 to £2,600. For the 2.0L B47D20A, rebuilt units range from £2,800 to £3,600.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a MINI Clubman Cooper D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timing chain stretch in the B47D20A engine often presents as a metallic rattling or tapping noise from the engine bay, particularly during cold starts.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older R55 MINI Clubman Cooper D?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's overall condition and current market value. An older R55 model is typically valued between £4,000 and £6,000.

mainEntity.name: How long does a MINI Clubman Cooper D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service typically takes 2 to 4 working days from the time the engine arrives at the specialist workshop.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the R55 and F54 MINI Clubman Cooper D engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The R55 (2007-2014) uses the 1.6L 9HZ (DV6TED4) PSA-developed diesel engine, producing around 109-112hp. The F54 (2015-2024) uses BMW's 2.0L B47D20A engine, producing 150hp.

historyTimeline.h2: MINI Clubman Cooper D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance

milestones.description: Minor emissions and mapping updates to the 9HZ (DV6TED4) to meet Euro 5 standards, maintaining similar power output.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the MINI Clubman Cooper D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: MINI Clubman Cooper D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The MINI Clubman Cooper D is generally reliable, but both the 1.6L 9HZ and 2.0L B47D20A engines have specific, well-documented wear points. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - Why the MINI Clubman Cooper D 9HZ (DV6TED4) Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Carbon build-up in the oil feed line restricts lubrication to the turbocharger, leading to premature bearing wear and eventual failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbo and clean oil feed lines.
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if the engine block is undamaged, but does not address underlying carbon issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the turbo failure has caused secondary damage to the engine block or pistons.

problems.recommendation: For early R55 models with high mileage, a targeted turbo repair or a quality used engine is often the most financially sensible route. For F54 models, if timing chain rattle is present, address it immediately with a chain kit replacement; if internal damage has already occurred, a rebuilt B47D20A engine is the only reliable long-term solution.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the MINI Clubman Cooper D B47D20A Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: While improved over the older N47 design, the B47 timing chain can still stretch over time, causing rattling noises on startup and potential catastrophic engine damage if it snaps.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, and tensioner.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable preventative measure if caught early before internal engine damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the chain has snapped or caused valve/piston damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. A typical older R55 MINI Clubman Cooper D (2007-2010) falls into the £4,000-£6,000 band, meaning a used engine or targeted repair is often the most economical choice, as a full rebuild may approach the vehicle's total value. Later F54 models (2015+) typically hold £8,000-£14,000, where a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a highly justifiable investment to protect the vehicle's residual value.
problems.recommendation: For early R55 models with high mileage, a targeted turbo repair or a quality used engine is often the most financially sensible route. For F54 models, if timing chain rattle is present, address it immediately with a chain kit replacement; if internal damage has already occurred, a rebuilt B47D20A engine is the only reliable long-term solution.

items.question: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a MINI Clubman Cooper D?
items.answer: Timing chain stretch in the B47D20A engine often presents as a metallic rattling or tapping noise from the engine bay, particularly during cold starts.
keyPoints: You may also experience a check engine light or reduced engine power.
Ignoring this noise can lead to catastrophic internal engine damage.
If you hear rattling, have the chain tension inspected immediately.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older R55 MINI Clubman Cooper D?
items.answer: It depends on the vehicle's overall condition and current market value. An older R55 model is typically valued between £4,000 and £6,000.
keyPoints: If the rest of the car is in excellent condition, a used or reconditioned engine can extend its life cost-effectively.
If the vehicle has multiple other faults, the replacement cost may exceed the car's value.
Always evaluate the full vehicle condition before committing to a rebuild.

items.question: How long does a MINI Clubman Cooper D engine replacement take?
items.answer: A professional supply and fit service typically takes 2 to 4 working days from the time the engine arrives at the specialist workshop.
keyPoints: This includes removing the old unit, fitting the replacement, and updating the ECU mapping.
Nationwide delivery of the engine can add 1-2 days to the overall timeline.
Complex variants like the Cooper D Exclusive may require additional calibration time.

items.question: What is the difference between the R55 and F54 MINI Clubman Cooper D engines?
items.answer: The R55 (2007-2014) uses the 1.6L 9HZ (DV6TED4) PSA-developed diesel engine, producing around 109-112hp. The F54 (2015-2024) uses BMW's 2.0L B47D20A engine, producing 150hp.
keyPoints: The B47D20A offers significantly more torque and better fuel efficiency.
The 9HZ is more prone to turbocharger oil starvation issues.
Parts and replacement engines are not interchangeable between these two generations.
